title: Borrowed Umbrella
stanzas: The bus shelter had one dry seat
and a man who stood instead of sitting,
holding an umbrella he had not opened.
He said, take it, I live two streets over.
I walked home through the covered market,
past the fish stall, past the flowers,
and it left a thin wet line
the whole length of the pavement.
In the hallway it stayed open
three days, ribs up like a tent
nobody slept in. The cloth dried
into a shape that was not mine.
Once, in March, I nearly took it back.
I got as far as his gate,
saw the kitchen light on, heard a radio
talking to an empty room.
It is on my hook still, black, ordinary,
one rib bent where the wind got under it.
When it rains I use it.
I have stopped calling it borrowed.
